core_phrases.irish: Tá mé ag dul go dtí an phictiúrlann amárach.
core_phrases.english: I am going to the cinema tomorrow.
core_phrases.pronunciation_tip: Taw may egg dull guh dee un fik-chure-lawn ah-mar-ahk.

core_phrases.irish: Beidh mé ag foghlaim Gaeilge ar líne an tseachtain seo chugainn.
core_phrases.english: I will be learning Irish online next week.
core_phrases.pronunciation_tip: Bay may egg foh-lim Gwayl-guh air leen-eh ahk tchok-in.

core_phrases.irish: Tá sé ceaptha go mbeidh an aimsir go hálainn ar an deireadh seachtaine.
core_phrases.english: It is expected that the weather will be beautiful at the weekend.
core_phrases.pronunciation_tip: Taw shay kyap-ha guh may vay an am-shir guh hawl-in air un der-ahk shokh-tawn-eh.

grammar_rule.title: Using 'Tá' and 'Beidh' for future tense
grammar_rule.explanation: Use 'Tá' for immediate future actions and 'Beidh' for future plans or predictions.
examples: Tá mé ag dul go dtí an siopa.
Beidh mé ag caint le mo chara amárach.

pronunciation_notes: In Irish, the future tense is formed using the verbs 'Tá' (is) and 'Beidh' (will be).
Pay attention to the slender and broad consonants for accurate pronunciation.
Practice linking words together smoothly for natural speech flow.

mini_task.instruction: Describe your plans for the upcoming weekend.
prompts: What will you be doing on Saturday?
Where do you plan to go on Sunday?
Who will you meet during the weekend?
